Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

remember verb

also recall, remember to, if I remember rightly, if my memory serves me right, if I remember right, if my memory serves me, as I recall, as a reminder, for the record

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.106: omnia meminit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 370

meminī, meminisse

verb: perfect in form with present sense; imperative mementō, mementōte

remember, keep in mind

What one remembers in the genitive or accusative, or as a clause; with a present infinitive for a scene one saw (meminī Catōnem mēcum disserere, Cic. Lael. 11, Lewis & Short). Mementō with an infinitive is “remember to …, be sure to …”; sī bene meminī, if I remember rightly (Traupman 106).

Other words

  • recordor, recordārī, recordātus sum — call to mind, recollect

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Verg. A. 3.107: sī rīte audīta recordor

  • memoriā tenēre — keep in mind, remember

    phrase: ablative of memoria with teneō · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 12; Caes. BG 1.14 (Lewis & Short, s.v. memoria); Traupman 370

  • commemorō, commemorāre, commemorāvī, commemorātum — go over in one’s mind; more often, mention

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 38: quid quōque diē dīxerim, audierim, ēgerim, commemorō vesperī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 157, 370

    Traupman gives it first for “remember”, but in Lewis & Short its usual sense is “recount, mention”, and “call to mind” is rare.

  • ut mea memoria est — as I recall, as far as I remember

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.31.4: ut mea memoria est (Lewis & Short s.v. memoria); Traupman 106: as I recall, ut mea memoria est

  • memoriae causā — as a reminder, to help the memory

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 1.19: sī quid memoriae causā rettulit in libellum (Lewis & Short s.v. libellus); Traupman 106: as a reminder, memoriae causā

Examples

  • «Meministīne?» «Meminī!»

    “Do you remember?” “I remember!”Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

  • aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem

    remember to keep a level head when things are hardHor. C. 2.3.1–2

  • sī meminī, fuerant tibi quattuor, Aelia, dentēs

    if I remember rightly, Aelia, you had four teethMart. 1.19.1

  • omnia quae cūrant meminērunt

    they remember everything they care aboutCic. Sen. 21

  • Sī ego satis commeminī …

    If my memory serves me right …Traupman 103

  • Sī bene meminī …

    If I remember right …Traupman 106
